newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - AUG 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - AUG 15.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- JARDINE ASKS ITS INVESTORS TO REPORT HOLDINGS

The Jardine Group UK conglomerate has written its member companies requesting they report their holdings, a move which follows the recent announcement Hong Kong businessman Li Ka-shing had acquired stakes in two of Jardine's main businesses. The request has prompted speculation Ka-shing may be preparing a bid for - or seeking an alliance with - Jardine, though Jardine corporate secretary Neil McNamara stated there had been no discussions relating to shareholdings in its companies since the initial talks with Ka-shing.
-- KOHL SIGNALS FURTHER COMPROMISES OVER TAX

German chancellor Helmut Kohl has indicated he may be willing to significantly reduce the government's planned tax reforms in a bid to overcome a parliamentary blockade by the Social Democratic party. Speaking to ZDF television, Kohl declared even if the reforms could not be initiated all at once, the government should 'at least do a part so that the country can see a future for itself'. The chancellor also stressed Theo Waigel's proposed cabinet reshuffle would give the coalition 'an additional boost'.
-- ACTIVISTS MAKING WAVES IN OIL RIG PROTEST

Greenpeace protestors are continuing their demonstration on the legs of the Stena Dee oil rig in Shetland, in an attempt to disrupt oil exploration at the Atlantic frontier. The environmental activists are protesting the continued burning of fossil fuels, claiming the process causes alterations in the climate, but critics have noted the site they are protesting only accounts for 0.5 per cent of the UK's annual output. Greenpeace claims, however, their central goal is to 'raise public awareness'.
-- US CATTLE RENDERERS PREPARE TO SUE BRUSSELS FOR $100M

The US rendering industry has announced plans to sue the European Commission for 64m stg over its new proposals to control the spread of 'mad cow' disease, unless a clause which could ban US exports of tallow is altered. Tallow, which is used in products from candles to painkillers, is a market with an estimated value of 67.7m stg per year, and pharmaceuticals and cosmetics manufacturers have warned the Commission its 'mad cow' proposals could lead to a lack of tallow supplies, forcing temporary shutdowns and product shortages within the industry.
-- SATELLITE DISTRIBUTOR FOR RADIO CALLS IN RECEIVERS

Satellite Media Services, the group owned by Capital Radio, the ABC US television company, Emap and Scottish Radio, and which distributes advertisements and programming to commercial radio, has gone into receivership. SMS was apparently no longer able to co-exist in a market consisting of companies such as Independent Media Distribution, which offered similar services, but via much cheaper ISDN lines. Noting its increased competition, and the lack of development in the UK radio market, SMS had recently begun to examine other markets, such as general data distribution.
-- INTERNET FOREIGN EXCHANGE PLANNED

UK high street travel agent Thomas Cook is planning to become the first company to sell foreign exchange via the Internet. Through its initiative, customers will be permitted to order foreign exchange via the company's Web site and pay for it by credit card. Once acquired, the cash will be transferred to the desired destination for a fee of 5 pounds stg. Management consultant Datamonitor estimates the value of on-line travel booking will have increased from 1m stg today to 1bn stg by 2002.
-- MILLENNIUM 'BOMB' LIFTS MICRO FOCUS

Micro Focus, the computer services group, has moved into the black in the first half after reporting a 21 per cent increase in sales. The results were boosted by demand for solutions to the so-called millennium 'time-bomb', which accounted for about 15 per cent of revenues. Micro Focus reported pre-tax profits of 5.17m stg for the six months to July 31, compared to losses of 9.46m stg last time.
-- NTL TAKES OUT 875M STG LOAN TO FUND CABLE AIMS

US cable and broadcasting services group NTL, which is thought to be in early-stage talks with UK cable company Telewest about a possible alliance to challenge Cable & Wireless Communications, has confirmed that it has arranged a new 875m stg eight-year syndicated loan underwritten by Chase Manhattan Bank. The company expects to use the bulk of the new loan to finance cable development and digital television ambitions.
-- RISE IN REVENUES FROM LICENCE AGREEMENTS SWEETENS MAID

Maid, the online business information company, has reported a halving of interim operating losses, to 1.71m stg, on turnover up 46 per cent at 14m stg. The results were boosted by a sharp rise in revenues from licence agreements to use the company's technology, with partners including CompuServe, Fujitsu and British Telecom. Maid chief executive Dan Wagner said he was 'highly confident' of meeting analysts' expectations of a move into operating profit in the second half.
-- 'CELTIC ALLIANCE' AS SCOTTISH MEDIA TAKES 15 PER CENT OF ULSTER TV

Newspaper and broadcasting group Scottish Media has spent over 14m stg to increase its stake in Ulster Television to 14.99 per cent. The move makes Scottish Media, owner of Scottish Television and The Herald newspaper, the largest single shareholder in Ulster and has been seen as a clear indication of its interest in the company. It is understood that Scottish, which is currently completing the 100m stg takeover of Grampian Television, moved because of concern that another media company had begun stake building in Ulster.
